Tool Service resources

Fields every OpenEngine resource shares. Resources follow Kubernetes conventions: apiVersion and kind say what a document is, metadata identifies it, spec holds what its author wants, and status, where a kind has one, is what the service observed. Applying a resource creates it under a new name and updates it under a known one; status and the service-set metadata fields are ignored on apply. Several resources may share one file, separated by ---.

Validate files with uv run python packages/contracts/tooling/resources.py check FILE… from v2/.

Tool

apiVersion: openengine.cc/v1alpha1 · kind: Tool · defined in tool_service/v1/resources/tool.schema.yaml

An invocable capability bound to one Connection. Agents call it on oe.v1.tools.invoke.{namespace}.{name}; the connection, the adapter operation and the trusted configuration are fixed here, so nothing an agent sends can choose another connection or override them. Applying validates the definition with its adapter and rejects a configuration the adapter cannot honour, including a recovery it does not implement. Calling a tool also needs a ToolGrant.

Example from github-issue-comment.yaml
apiVersion: openengine.cc/v1alpha1
kind: Tool
metadata:
  name: github-issue-comment
  namespace: default
  labels:
    provider: github
spec:
  description: Add a comment to an issue in the OpenEngine repository.
  connectionRef:
    name: github-openengine
  executor:
    adapter: nango
    operation: github-issue-comment
  inputSchema:
    type: object
    additionalProperties: false
    required: [issueNumber, body]
    properties:
      issueNumber:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
      body:
        type: string
        minLength: 1
  outputSchema:
    type: object
    required: [commentId, url]
    properties:
      commentId:
        type: string
      url:
        type: string
  configuration:
    repository: spiralsoft/openengine
  execution:
    timeoutSeconds: 60
    recovery: reconcile
    maxAttempts: 3
status:
  phase: Ready
  observedGeneration: 1

FieldTypeDescription

ToolGrant

apiVersion: openengine.cc/v1alpha1 · kind: ToolGrant · defined in tool_service/v1/resources/toolgrant.schema.yaml

Lets one workspace, or one step execution in it, call one tool. Only trusted control-plane callers may apply or delete grants. The Graph Engine is the usual one: a Graph step's agent.tools lists the tools it may call. Once a step attempt has its workspace, and before sending the attempt to run there, the Graph Engine applies a grant for each tool to that attempt in that workspace, and deletes them when the attempt ends. Starting a step that lists tools therefore needs the tool service to be available. A missing, expired or deleted grant denies the call, and grants are checked again just before every dispatch. A grant is bound to the tool as it was when the grant was applied: a tool deleted and created again under the same name has a new uid, and the old grant does not cover it.

Example from github-issue-comment.yaml
apiVersion: openengine.cc/v1alpha1
kind: ToolGrant
metadata:
  name: reviewer-comment-access
  namespace: default
spec:
  subject:
    workspaceRef:
      name: review-job-88
    stepAttemptId: stepa_88_review_1
  toolRef:
    name: github-issue-comment
  constraints:
    issueNumbers: [42]
  expiresAt: "2026-10-22T00:00:00Z"
status:
  phase: Active
  toolUid: tool-uid-123

ToolGrantSpec

Who may call which tool, within what limits, until when.

FieldTypeDescription

toolRefrequiredNameRefThe Tool in the grant's namespace.
constraintsobjectLimits on the arguments, such as issueNumbers: [42]. Their shape is the tool's adapter's to define; it validates them when the grant is applied and enforces them on every call.

expiresAtstringAfter this UTC time the grant denies every call. Omitted means it does not expire.
Pattern ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]{1,9})?Z$. Format date-time.

ToolInvocation

apiVersion: openengine.cc/v1alpha1 · kind: ToolInvocation · defined in tool_service/v1/resources/toolinvocation.schema.yaml

The durable record of one tool call. The service creates it when a call on oe.v1.tools.invoke.{namespace}.{name} is accepted, and owns its status; it cannot be applied, so nobody can forge its identity or authorization. The tool comes from the subject and the workspace from the caller's verified credentials. The resolved tool definition is stored with it, so changing the Tool later cannot change accepted work. Its result is read through oe.v1.toolinvocations.get, never from events.

Example from github-issue-comment.yaml
apiVersion: openengine.cc/v1alpha1
kind: ToolInvocation
metadata:
  name: ti-123
  namespace: default
  uid: invocation-uid-123
  generation: 1
spec:
  toolRef:
    name: github-issue-comment
    uid: tool-uid-123
    generation: 1
  workspaceRef:
    name: review-job-88
  workspaceGeneration: 3
  stepAttemptId: stepa_88_review_1
  arguments:
    issueNumber: 42
    body: Review complete.
status:
  phase: Accepted
  authorization:
    grantRefs:
      - name: reviewer-comment-access
        uid: grant-uid-123
  attemptCount: 0
